*2027 Budget: Higher spending, but will tax increases follow?*
The 2027 Appropriation Bill points to a 12% rise in primary expenditure, led by a 27% increase in capex. Strong 2026 revenue has helped, but easing vehicle imports could slow revenue growth. We expect a focus on broadening the tax base rather than major tax increases.

Hayleys Retail Holdings Ltd has selected supply chain software provider Blue Yonder to build its grocery retail operations from the ground up, the two companies said in a joint statement.

The Government’s Budget recorded a surplus of Rs. 22.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, reversing a deficit of Rs. 441.4 billion a year earlier, as revenue from motor vehicle imports drove a 20% increase in collections that outran a slower rise in spending.

Banking sector credit-to-deposit ratio tops 70% for first time in three years
Sri Lanka’s banking sector Credit-to-Deposit Ratio (CDR) has exceeded 70% for the first time in three years, reaching 74.0% by end June 2026 and surpassing its long-term average, with the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) flagging credit growth outpacing deposits and a widening credit gap as potential sources of systemic risk.
